items.new_text: Apply the `definirPapelDoMembro` guard here too: removing the last active admin
would leave nobody able to assign the role again.

Change the role of an unused invite. Blip uses the same `definirPapelDoMembro` operation because invitees are already `tenant-user` rows and `set .../role` applies equally. Here they live in `convite`, so a separate function has the same effect: the new role applies at first sign-in.

Always show the contract summary: source `tenant-summary` is readable by all three roles. Pipe calculates both counts in the database for every viewer. In the source `tenant.applications` stays `[]`, so 'Chatbots' is absent in practice, and `members` loads only for `admin` with the subscription.
Cancel an open invitation by expiring, not deleting it. Keep the row as evidence of who invited whom; expiry invalidates its link, as `criarConvite` does before issuing a replacement.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
Run one query at a time: a transaction has one connection, and concurrent queries can interfere, as noted in `lib/portal.ts`.
One of three ACCOUNT roles (`papel.escopo = 'conta'`, migration 0021). `nome` is source `roleId` (`admin`, `member`, `guest`), which `PAPEIS_DA_ORIGEM` maps to label, description and icon.

Record the source table for this row. Blip uses one `tenant-user` table and `userStatus` distinguishes `Accepted` from `PendingUser`; Pipe stores accepted users in `usuario` and pending invitees in `convite`.

Queue colors are customer data recognized in Desk, but selection is closed rather than arbitrary hex. Use the extended `@pipe/ui` palette (`TEMA.grafico.serie`), which can carry hue without implying status. Store the token NAME in `fila.cor`, never hex, so palette changes update existing queues without Management color literals.

Return the stored color's `var()` or `null` when it is outside the palette. Older seed rows stored raw hex in `fila.cor`; they stay readable as text but get no color dot, since using raw hex would violate the palette. Later registration replaces those values.
The resource governing the Team tab itself.

Source `selectAllPermissions()` uses the top-level role to fill lower radios. Only `personalizado` reads screen-selected entries; other levels determine the map, avoiding stored permissions that contradict the displayed role.
Ignore keys unknown to the source; reject an invalid level rather than silently accepting it.
`ler` is satisfied by `escrever`; `escrever` is not satisfied by `ler`.
Duplicate `EDITAR_FLUXO` here deliberately: `ciclo-de-vida-do-fluxo.ts` now imports `exigirPermissaoNoFluxo`; importing its constant back would create a module cycle.
Split `<recurso>.<verbo>` into its two parts or reject a programming error.

Authorize THIS flow's permission or its account equivalent, matching `exigirPermissao` in `sessao.ts` and the second gate in research §4.3. `codigo` is a source `<recurso>.<verbo>` such as `builder.escrever`, `channels.ler`, or `team.escrever`. Permit a flow member with the requested resource level (`admin` grants all) OR an account member with `EQUIVALENTE_NA_CONTA`. Check the flow's unique-key row first, then the account's `exists` with two joins; many tenants have no flow membership rows.
Check the same permission without throwing, so the screen can decide what to render.

The contact Team tab mirrors source `/team` and PER-FLOW RBAC. Source `getUsersAccounts` (`/applications/{shortName}@msging.net/users/accounts`) combines with `getApplicationUsersPermissions` (`.../permissions`) per contact in `TeamController._loadMembers`; research `referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-identidade-tenant-permissao.md` §3 records 'a permissão não é do tenant, é do bot'. Contract membership is prerequisite, as the source says: 'Essa pessoa não faz parte do contrato. O administrador deve incluir a pessoa no contrato antes de adicioná-la ao chatbot.'. The role slider (`team.addUserModal.slider`: `visualize`, `custom`, `edit`, `admin`) fills per-resource radios (`PermissionsList.html`: `none` 0, `read` 1, `readWrite` 3) through `selectAllPermissions()`; only custom grants are edited individually. Store the full permission map via `permissoesDoPapel`. Team edits pass `team.escrever` ON THE FLOW or `automacao.fluxo.editar` ON THE ACCOUNT through `exigirPermissaoNoFluxo`. Requiring only flow admin would lock out tenants with no existing members; requiring only account permission would discard per-flow granularity.
List members like `TeamController._loadMembers()`. Viewing the team requires `team.ler`, because the edit modal exposes each member's permissions to contact administrators, not every participant.
Return what the contact menu may show, including when the user is not a member.
Blip hides actions for `owner` (`ng-if="!user.owner"`). Pipe has no owner role, so numerically prevent a contact from losing its last administrator.

Source `confirmAddUser()` first invites non-contract users as `guest`. Pipe keeps invitation separate at `POST /v1/convites` in `dominio/convites.ts`; it starts its own transaction and returns a copyable link because Pipe sends no email. Use the source refusal text and let the screen offer invitation afterward.
The edit modal's 'Salvar alterações'; write nothing when no values changed.

Flatten to one field per resource because `diferenca` compares with `===`: equal maps are different objects, so nested values would make every Save appear changed. Flattening also names the changed permission row in the log.
`removeUser()` includes a last-administrator guard absent from the source.

Rows follow source `PermissionsList.html` order (`payments`, `channels`, `desk`, `users`, `basicConfigurations`, `connectionInformations`, `resources`, `growth`, `logMessages`, `builder`, `analysis`) and use pt-BR titles under `modules.application.detail.permissions.*.title`. Omit `iaModel`/`iaEnhancement`/`iaProviders` because AI was removed from `apps/gestao-vite/src/paginas/fluxo/itens.ts`, and omit untitled `scheduler`. Add `team` from `permissions.team.title` to govern this screen, although the source template lacks it.

Map each flow resource to an equivalent ACCOUNT permission for the second authorization gate. Currently all map to `automacao.fluxo.editar`: catalog 0019 has only 'Cria e edita chatbots', with no separate `automacao.fluxo.ler` (`paginas/fluxo/equipe/permissoes.ts`). Keep this mapping central so future account permissions for `desk` or `payments` do not require route changes.
Template text was not typed by the agent either; report it in the same separate column.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.

Agent effort report, design §4.4. `packages/core/src/esforco/` owns the calculation: 200 typed characters/minute, 1,000 read characters/minute, audio at 1×, and quick-reply/template text excluded from effort and shown in a separate column. This module fetches inputs and sums core results.
Effort divided by tickets; weighted by construction (metrics spec §5).
Text the agent did NOT type: quick replies and templates.
Effort this text would add if counted as typing.
Conversations closed in the period without effort from any agent.
Load messages from conversations closed in the period with audio attachments:
without attachment duration, the effort model cannot measure listening or speaking.
Timestamps of each agent's outgoing messages form the session-time basis.
Convert PostgreSQL `time` output `HH:MM:SS` to `HH:MM`.

Validate `HH:MM`, allowing `24:00` because core treats it as next-day midnight. Share validation between `acoes/regras.ts` creation and `cadastros.ts` range/exception editing to prevent divergent copies.
Format long report durations as `4h 12min`. Round total minutes, not the remainder after hours: rounding 7,190 seconds' remainder alone yielded `1h 60min` instead of carrying into the hour.
Duration as `mm:ss`, or `hh:mm:ss` above one hour; use a dash for null.
Show the metric denominator in text, e.g. '289 de 312 · 23 sem resposta'. Metrics spec §2 rejects an average hiding its denominator, because that average can improve when service worsens.
`en-CA` yields `YYYY-MM-DD`, accepted by `<input type="date">`.

Validate both URL filters BEFORE querying: pasted links, old bookmarks and bots are untrusted input. Without validation, `?fila=abc` reaches PostgreSQL as `abc::uuid` and makes the whole screen return 500. Invalid values become `undefined`, meaning no filter, so the screen opens with all rows. Keep this in pure `formato.ts`, which these screens already import and which knows `YYYY-MM-DD`.
`YYYY-MM-DD` accepted by PostgreSQL; it still rejects impossible dates such as 31/02.

Use Sunday = 0, matching PostgreSQL `extract(dow)` and core `getUTCDay`. Define it here, not in `cadastros.ts`: the schedule form is a client component, and importing that module would pull Drizzle and the PostgreSQL pool into the browser bundle.
Total customer wait runs until the answer, or until closure when unanswered.

Group the history list by queue, agent, label or outcome instead of creating six unused Reports screens for the same cuts. A distinct report screen is needed only for a different axis, such as Effort's character and audio counts. Group the already loaded page, not SQL's full population: `carregarHistorico` caps results at `LIMITE_HISTORICO`, and grouping more rows than the screen displays would mislead.

Group loaded rows by the selected column while retaining order within groups. A conversation appears under each of its labels, so group totals intentionally exceed row count: the question is how many conversations touched each label, not how to partition the total.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
History of closed conversations. As in monitoring, derive status and durations from `evento_atendimento` through `@pipe/core`, never from the mutable conversation field.
Limit rows because history is for lookup, not export.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.

Read setup-wizard signals through the application database role with session-tenant RLS. Use one transaction with short SERIAL queries: `Promise.all` inside `comTenant` can clear `pipe.tenant_id`. Step meanings live in `passos-da-implantacao.ts`; this module only queries the database.
Use the tenant time zone for card 'today', not the server time zone.
Compute current-day bounds in the tenant time zone with PostgreSQL, which knows the time-zone database; duplicating daylight-saving logic in JavaScript risks losing a whole day.
From the start of `de` through the inclusive end of `ate`, as calendar days in the account time zone.
Instant range in the account time zone, equivalent to Management's `Janela` in `lib/banco.ts`.
Maximum possible load: full capacity occupied by conversations waiting for an agent.
Management may read any tenant ticket; Desk may read only tickets assigned to that agent.
An internal note is the supervisor-agent conversation opened by the source bubble; it must not reach the customer.
Derive a readable ticket number from UUID because the model has no separate sequence.
Read everything monitoring needs in one transaction. Pass `agora` so running real-time counters use one instant across cards; otherwise card totals disagree with the table.

Order the WAITING QUEUE by priority, then oldest first. The source requires low priority (`baixa`) before no priority (`sem_prioridade`); when the column defaulted to medium, priority had not been chosen, so the list used creation time alone. Oldest-first ties prevent the queue from becoming a stack. Assigned/in-progress tickets still use creation order because priority no longer changes who serves them.
